equation.label: Left-Endpoint Approximation
equation.formula: $$A \approx L_{n} = f\left( x_{0} \right)\text{Δ}x + f\left( x_{1} \right)\text{Δ}x + \text{⋯} + f\left( x_{n - 1} \right)\text{Δ}x = {\sum\limits_{i = 1}^{n}{f\left( x_{i - 1} \right)\text{Δ}x}}$$

equation.label: Right-Endpoint Approximation
equation.formula: $$A \approx R_{n} = f\left( x_{1} \right)\text{Δ}x + f\left( x_{2} \right)\text{Δ}x + \text{⋯} + f\left( x_{n} \right)\text{Δ}x = {\sum\limits_{i = 1}^{n}{f\left( x_{i} \right)\text{Δ}x}}$$

equation.label: Properties of the Definite Integral
equation.formula: $$\int_{a}^{a}{f(x)dx = 0}$$ $${\int_{b}^{a}{f(x)dx}} = \text{−}{\int_{a}^{b}{f(x)dx}}$$ $${\int_{a}^{b}{\left\lbrack {f(x) + g(x)} \right\rbrack dx}} = {\int_{a}^{b}{f(x)dx}} + {\int_{a}^{b}{g(x)dx}}$$ $$\int_{a}^{b}{\left\lbrack {f(x) - g(x)} \right\rbrack dx = {\int_{a}^{b}{f(x)dx - {\int_{a}^{b}{g(x)dx}}}}}$$ $${\int_{a}^{b}{cf(x)dx}} = c{\int_{a}^{b}{f(x)}}$$ for constant c $${\int_{a}^{b}{f(x)dx}} = {\int_{a}^{c}{f(x)dx}} + {\int_{c}^{b}{f(x)dx}}$$

equation.label: Mean Value Theorem for Integrals
equation.formula: If $$f(x)$$ is continuous over an interval $$\left\lbrack {a,b} \right\rbrack,$$ then there is at least one point $$c \in \left\lbrack {a,b} \right\rbrack$$ such that $$f(c) = \frac{1}{b - a}{\int_{a}^{b}{f(x)dx}}.$$

equation.label: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus Part 1
equation.formula: If $$f(x)$$ is continuous over an interval $$\left\lbrack {a,b} \right\rbrack,$$ and the function $$F(x)$$ is defined by $$F(x) = {\int_{a}^{x}{f(t)dt}},$$ then $$F^{\prime}\left. \text{(}x \right) = f(x).$$

equation.label: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus Part 2
equation.formula: If f is continuous over the interval $$\left\lbrack {a,b} \right\rbrack$$ and $$F(x)$$ is any antiderivative of $$f(x),$$ then $${\int_{a}^{b}{f(x)dx = F(b) - F(a)}}.$$

equation.label: Integration Formulas Involving Logarithmic Functions
equation.formula: $$\int{x^{-1}dx = \text{ln}|x| + C}$$ $$\int{\text{ln}\mspace{2mu} x\ dx = x\mspace{2mu}\text{ln}\mspace{2mu} x - x + C = x\left( {\text{ln}\mspace{2mu} x - 1} \right) + C}$$ $$\int{\text{log}_{a}\ x\ dx = \frac{x}{\text{ln}\mspace{2mu} a}\left( {\text{ln}\mspace{2mu} x - 1} \right) + C}$$

equation.label: Integrals That Produce Inverse Trigonometric Functions
equation.formula: $$\left. \int{\frac{du}{\sqrt{a^{2} - u^{2}}} = \text{sin}^{-1}\left( \frac{u}{a} \right) + C} \right.$$ $$\left. \int{\frac{du}{a^{2} + u^{2}} = \frac{1}{a}\mspace{1mu}\text{tan}^{-1}\left( \frac{u}{a} \right) + C} \right.$$ $$\left. \int{\frac{du}{u\sqrt{u^{2} - a^{2}}} = \frac{1}{a}\mspace{1mu}\text{sec}^{-1}\left( \frac{u}{a} \right) + C} \right.$$
